THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF THE MV ACT  1988, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED  12.06.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.1512/2016 ON THE FILE OF PRL.
 SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS  TRIBUNAL, SAUNDATTI, AS COMPENSATION AWARDED IS EXCESSIVE  AND EXORBITANT BY ALLOWING THIS APPEAL & ETC.
 THIS MFA COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS   JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 CORAM:
THE HON'BLE
DR . JUSTICE K.MANMADHA RAO  -2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:56
MFA No. 103432 of 2018 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act') by the NWKRTC (hereinafter referred to as 'the Corporation' for short) challenging by the Judgment and Award dated 12.06.2018 passed in MVC No.1512/2016 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Saundatti.
2. For convenience, the parties are referred to, based on their rankings before the Tribunal.

3. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are as under:
On 08.08.2015 at about 1.30 p.m., on Saundatti- Ramdurg road, situated at the land of Siddappa Ramappa Gudagar, the petitioner the petitioner was inmate as passenger of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42/F-1595.
The driver of the bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the bus and it toppled down at the spot of the accident.
Due to the said impact, the NC: 2026:KHC-D:56 HC-KAR petitioner and other inmates of the bus sustained grievous injuries.

After the accident, the petitioner and others were shifted to the Government Hospital,
Saundatti for treatment and thereafter they took treatment in private hospitals.
At the time of the accident, the petitioner was studying in 7th standard.
Due to the accident, it caused impact on the functional and IQ strategy of the petitioner.
The petitioner spent huge amount towards her treatment.

The petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act claiming compensation of Rs.11,80,000/-.
4.
In response to court notice, the respondent appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
It is stated that claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

It is contended that the petitioners were not at all traveled in the bus and sustained The Divisional Manager vs Basanagouda S/O Kenchappa Chulaki on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11595634/
2 any grievous injuries or fracture.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Basanagouda S/O Kenchappa Chulaki
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have taken undue advantage of the accident and filed the claim NC: 2026:KHC-D:56 HC-KAR petitions in order to grab compensation by showing their wrong age, occupation, income description of injuries, medical expenses etc.,
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petitions.
5. The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings of the parties, framed issues.
The natural guardian of the petitioner was examined as P.W.1, examined the doctor as P.W.2 and got marked documents Exs.P1 to Ex.P17.
On the other hand, the driver of the bus was examined as R.W.1 and did not produce any documents on his behalf.

The Tribunal after assessing the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.1,19,601.50 with interest at the rate of 9% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
6. The Corporation, aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, filed this Miscellaneous First Appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:56 HC-KAR 7.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant- Corporation and the learned counsel for the respondent- claimant.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant-Corporation submits that he does not dispute the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, however, insofar as the interest awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, the same shall be reduced to 6% p.a. instead of 9% p.a. awarded by the Tribunal.
9. Learned counsel for the respondent-claimant submits that he has not objection for the same.

10. In view of the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties, and in view of the decision rendered by this court in MFA NO.5896/2018 C/W MFA NO.4444/2018 AND MFA NO.4659/2018 in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS VS VENKATESHAN V AND OTHERS, wherein a similar question arose with regard to awarding of interest, keeping in view Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, it has been held that rate of interest shall NC: 2026:KHC-D:56 HC-KAR not exceed 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

entities.text: MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS VS VENKATESHAN V AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case also, the rate of interest is reduced to 6% p.a. instead of 9% p.a. awarded by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by reducing the interest to 6% p.a. instead of 9% p.a. awarded by the Tribunal.
iii) The rest of the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
